Before you begin
How to navigate the fundus
①
Dial in your focus first
Before you try to identify anything, use the lens wheel (or scroll) to bring the image into sharp focus. Find a vessel and adjust until its edges are crisp and clear. The correct power compensates for the patient's refractive error — a blurry image will cause you to miss subtle findings.
②
Find a blood vessel
Once focused, scan slowly until you see a dark line against the red reflex — that is a retinal vessel. It does not matter which one you find first.
③
Trace towards the bifurcations
Follow the vessel and watch for where it splits into two branches — a bifurcation. The branches always point away from the optic disc. Turn around and follow the vessel in the opposite direction — towards where the branches converge — and you will arrive at the disc.
④
Anchor at the disc, then sweep outward
Once you locate the disc, use it as your landmark. Trace each arcade vessel outward — superior temporal, inferior temporal, then the nasal vessels. Finally, move two disc diameters temporal to find the macula.
